q: Poincaré-Bendixson theorem classifies limit sets of trajectories in the plane. For a bounded trajectory in ℝ² with no equilibria in its omega-limit set:
opts: The trajectory converges to a fixed point
The omega-limit set is a periodic orbit
The trajectory is dense in ℝ²
exp: Poincaré-Bendixson: in ℝ² (or S²), if the omega-limit set ω(x) is compact, connected, and contains no equilibrium, it must be a periodic orbit. This limits complexity of 2D ODEs—chaos is impossible in the plane.
